prompt.context_jp: 折原幸人との週末の約束が決まったばかりで、その声____いつになく弾んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 折原幸人との週末の約束が決まったばかりで、その声＿＿いつになく弾んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits after 「その声」 as the topic of this descriptive sentence.

feedback.correct_en: 「その声」 is already known/established (Etsuko on the phone), and the narrator is commenting on it as the topic — so は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 「その声」 as new information, which clashes with the already-established context. を would mark a direct object, which doesn't fit this intransitive description.

contrast_examples.en: Her voice (as for it) was lively.
A voice could be heard from somewhere. (new info — が)

prompt.context_jp: すぐそばに人の気配____あることに、彼女はまだ気づいていなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: すぐそばに人の気配＿＿あることに、彼女はまだ気づいていなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct particle for 「人の気配」 inside this embedded clause.

feedback.correct_en: 「人の気配がある」 introduces the existence of someone's presence as new information — が marks this new existential subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 「人の気配」 a contrasted topic, which is awkward inside the こと-clause. に doesn't fit the ある construction here.

contrast_examples.en: Someone is in the room. (new existence — が)
That person has already left. (topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 中身が大事じゃないなんて ひと言も言ってないよ ただ私____ 外見も大事でしょって 言ってるわけ
prompt.prompt_jp: ただ私＿＿、外見も大事でしょって言ってるわけ。
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko is contrasting her view with others'. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Contrastive は: 'as for ME (in contrast to others), I'm saying appearance also matters.' This is classic contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 「私」 new information or exhaustively identify her, which doesn't fit this contrastive self-assertion. も would mean 'me too,' which changes the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: そこへ突然、書籍編集部の貝塚八郎____息を切らして駆け込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこへ突然、書籍編集部の貝塚八郎＿＿息を切らして駆け込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka is introduced to the scene for the first time. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Kaizuka bursts onto the scene as new information — が marks newly-introduced subjects in narrative description.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Kaizuka is an already-established topic, but he's just appearing. を doesn't fit this intransitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアはもう閉まっている。
contrast_examples.en: The door is already closed. (established topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 四条真理恵先生の本____丸川賞の候補に入ったぞ！
prompt.prompt_jp: 四条真理恵先生の本＿＿丸川賞の候補に入ったぞ！
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka bursts in with breaking news. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is breaking news — the whole event (the book being nominated) is new information. が presents the entire fact freshly.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame 「先生の本」 as an already-known topic, deflating the excited newsflash tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生の本が賞を取った！
contrast_examples.en: Teacher's book won the prize! (breaking news — が)

contrast_examples.jp: 先生の本はいつも面白い。
contrast_examples.en: Teacher's books are always interesting. (topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 他社出版の本でも 受賞すれば ウチで出す先生の本____ 売れるんだよ
prompt.prompt_jp: 他社出版の本でも、受賞すれば、ウチで出す先生の本＿＿売れるんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: The speaker contrasts 'our company's book' with the other publisher's. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 「も」 (also) fits because he's saying 'even the books OUR company publishes will ALSO sell' — adding to the prize-winning book.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be odd here because the sentence is building an 'also' logic off the prize win. を doesn't fit intransitive 売れる.

contrast_examples.en: OUR book will sell. (identifying — different nuance)

prompt.context_jp: 招待の重みを最も感じているの____、二十年来のファンだと自認する藤岩である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 招待の重みを最も感じているの＿＿、二十年来のファンだと自認する藤岩である。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「感じているの」 in this identifying/cleft sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic Aのは B pattern: 'The one who feels it most is Fujiwa.' は marks the topic being identified.
feedback.incorrect_en: が could appear in a reverse cleft (BがAのだ), but with 〜である at the end, は is the natural topicalizer.

prompt.context_jp: 茸原____普段どおりのんびりと笑みを浮かべ、成り行きを楽しんでいるようにも見えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 茸原＿＿普段どおりのんびりと笑みを浮かべ、成り行きを楽しんでいるようにも見えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle to mark Kinohara in this description.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator contrasts Kinohara's calm reaction with the others' tension — contrastive/topical は works perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark Kinohara as newly introduced info, but he's already part of the established cast in the room.

contrast_examples.en: He was the one who calmed them.

prompt.context_jp: スーツ____ いかなる場所においても 正装です
prompt.prompt_jp: スーツ＿＿、いかなる場所においても正装です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in this general-statement sentence.

feedback.correct_en: は marks 「スーツ」 as the general topic: 'As for suits, they are formal wear anywhere.' This is a definitional statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify a specific suit as new info, which clashes with the generic meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 悦子の指先____、まるで長年その仕事を患ってきた職人のように迷いがない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 悦子の指先＿＿、まるで長年その仕事を患ってきた職人のように迷いがない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「悦子の指先」.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator makes Etsuko's fingertips the topic of description. は fits this characterizing sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would feel abrupt and suggest 'it is her fingertips that have no hesitation' (exhaustive listing), out of tone with the descriptive narration.

prompt.context_jp: 鏡越しに目____合うと、藤岩は微かに息を呑む。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏡越しに目＿＿合うと、藤岩は微かに息を呑む。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the set phrase 「目___合う」.

feedback.correct_en: 「目が合う」 is a fixed expression — the eyes meeting is an event occurring, taking が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the set phrase. を would require 「目を合わせる」 (active) — different verb and meaning.

contrast_examples.en: I made eye contact with him. (active)

prompt.context_jp: もう あんまり若くない人の前で 言うセリフ____ないよね
prompt.prompt_jp: もうあんまり若くない人の前で言うセリフ＿＿ないよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko contrasts: that's NOT a line to say in front of her. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 「〜ではない」 with the contrastive は softens into 'that's not the kind of line...' — a natural negated predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: がない would mean 'there is no line,' misreading the structure. をない isn't grammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: テツパン____ 鉄のパンツ いわゆる貞操帯のこと
prompt.prompt_jp: テツパン＿＿鉄のパンツ、いわゆる貞操帯のこと。
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko is defining a term. Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 「〜とは」 is the standard definitional topicalizer: 'The term X means...' — perfect for Etsuko's lecture.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just assert new info about the term, not define it. には is a locative/dative that doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 校閲とは文章を直す仕事だ。
contrast_examples.en: 'Proofreading' means the job of correcting writing.

prompt.context_jp: 真の意味____ 真逆だから
prompt.prompt_jp: 真の意味＿＿真逆だから。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for the true meaning, it's the opposite' — topicalizing 「真の意味」 to contrast with the surface/false meaning. は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively point to 'the true meaning' as what is opposite, less natural in the flow.

prompt.context_jp: ファンの方々____いなければ とっくに 書くのを やめてたと思います
prompt.prompt_jp: ファンの方々＿＿いなければ、とっくに書くのをやめてたと思います。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this conditional.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the 〜ば conditional with existence verb いる, が naturally marks the subject: 'if fans didn't exist...'
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a subordinate conditional clause is unnatural here — it would force a topical/contrastive reading in a slot that wants plain subject marking.

contrast_examples.en: If you weren't here, I'd be in trouble.

contrast_examples.jp: 君はいつも助けてくれる。

prompt.context_jp: 好きだからこそ できることって 絶対にある____思うんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 好きだからこそできること＿＿絶対にあると思うんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「できること」.

feedback.correct_en: Casual topic marker 「って」 (= というのは/は) fits Etsuko's conversational style: 'things you can do precisely because you love it — those definitely exist.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を would suggest an object of 思う, misreading the structure. に doesn't fit.

prompt.context_jp: 歩調____いつもより軽く、鞄を持つ腕さえ弾むように揺れる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 歩調＿＿いつもより軽く、鞄を持つ腕さえ弾むように揺れる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 「歩調」.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator characterizes Etsuko's walking pace as a topic ('her pace was lighter than usual'). は is right for this characterizing comparison.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the pace as new info, but it's a general description of her state, not an event.

contrast_examples.en: Today, the sky is blue. (描写 — が inside, は as frame)

prompt.context_jp: そのとき、後ろから聞き覚えのある声____自分の名を呼んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: そのとき、後ろから聞き覚えのある声＿＿自分の名を呼んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 「聞き覚えのある声」.

feedback.correct_en: A new voice suddenly appears from behind — classic new-information が for a sensed event.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly imply the voice was already a topic. を doesn't work because 声 is the subject of 呼んだ here, not its object.

contrast_examples.en: A dog barked somewhere. (new event — が)
That dog is ours. (known topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: お互い忙しくて ＿＿＿ 会えてないけどね
prompt.prompt_jp: お互い忙しくて＿＿＿会えてないけどね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits Etsuko's casual complaint about not seeing her boyfriend much.

feedback.correct_en: 「あんまり〜ない」 (not really/not much) fits casual speech about seeing someone infrequently.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「ぜんぜん」 means 'not at all' — too absolute; she's saying they meet rarely, not never. 「めっきり」 is used for changes over time ('markedly'), not for 'not often.'

prompt.context_jp: この世間の風潮に ＿＿＿ ならないだけ
prompt.prompt_jp: この世間の風潮に＿＿＿ならないだけ。
prompt.prompt_en: Etsuko can't stand the social trend. Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 「我慢ならない」 is a set phrase meaning 'cannot stand/tolerate' — exactly Etsuko's frustration here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「遠慮ならない」 isn't a standard phrase (遠慮 = restraint). 「油断ならない」 exists but means 'can't let one's guard down,' which doesn't fit frustration at a trend.

contrast_examples.jp: 失礼な態度に我慢ならない。
あいつは油断ならない。

prompt.context_jp: ＿＿＿ こと言うな せめて あやかり商法と言え
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿こと言うな。せめてあやかり商法と言え。
prompt.prompt_en: Kaizuka objects to calling it 'piggyback marketing.' Fill in the idiomatic expression.

feedback.correct_en: 「人聞きの悪い」 means 'sounding bad to others / making it sound worse than it is' — exactly fitting his protest.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「気持ちの悪い」 = creepy/disgusting (physical reaction). 「機嫌の悪い」 = bad-tempered (describes mood). Neither fits an objection to how something is phrased.

contrast_examples.jp: 人聞きの悪いこと言うなよ。
contrast_examples.en: Don't phrase it in a way that sounds bad.

prompt.context_jp: 私のような者が待ち会になど ＿＿＿ て
prompt.prompt_jp: 私のような者が待ち会になど＿＿＿くて。
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiwa humbly declines. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 「恐れ多い」 expresses deep humility — 'it would be too presumptuous for someone like me.' Matches Fujiwa's formal self-deprecation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「もったいない」 means 'wasteful/too good for me' and could work in other humility contexts but is less formal here. 「めずらしい」 means 'rare' and doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.en: Your words are too kind for me.

contrast_examples.jp: こんな高価なもの、もったいないです。
contrast_examples.en: Something this expensive is wasted on me.

prompt.context_jp: ＿＿＿ でもないこと 言わないでください！
prompt.prompt_jp: ＿＿＿でもないこと言わないでください！
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiwa scolds the intern for mentioning the possibility of losing. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 「縁起でもない」 is a set phrase: 'don't jinx it / don't say such ominous things.' Perfect for warding off bad luck before the award announcement.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「気でもない」 isn't a standard phrase. 「仕方でもない」 doesn't exist (仕方ない is different).

contrast_examples.jp: 縁起でもないこと言うな。

prompt.context_jp: 外見を 飾らなければならないほど⇒ 中身 ＿＿＿ ではありませんので
prompt.prompt_jp: 外見を飾らなければならないほど、中身＿＿＿ではありませんので。
prompt.prompt_en: Fujiwa snaps back about her inner self. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 「空っぽ」 (empty) collocates naturally with 「中身」 — 'my insides aren't empty enough that I need to decorate my outside.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 「貧しい」 (poor) is used for material wealth or spirit, but 中身が空っぽ is the idiomatic pairing. 「寂しい」 (lonely) doesn't fit 中身.

prompt.context_jp: このたびは ＿＿＿ 素晴らしい賞を頂きまして
prompt.prompt_jp: このたびは＿＿＿素晴らしい賞を頂きまして。
prompt.prompt_en: Shijo gives her humble acceptance speech. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 「身に余る」 = 'more than I deserve' — the standard humble acceptance phrase for honors.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「手に余る」 = 'beyond my ability to handle' (negative). 「目に余る」 = 'too much to overlook / outrageous' (negative). Both would be insulting to say about an award.

contrast_examples.en: It is an honor beyond my worth.

prompt.context_jp: もし よかったら 一緒に ＿＿＿ かきませんか？
prompt.prompt_jp: もしよかったら、一緒に＿＿＿かきませんか？
prompt.prompt_en: Yukito invites Etsuko to work out together. Fill in.

feedback.correct_en: 「汗をかく」 (to sweat/work out) is the standard collocation and matches the invite to exercise together.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「涙をかく」 isn't natural (涙を流す is used). 「息をかく」 isn't a collocation — you'd say 息をする or 息を切らす.

contrast_examples.en: Work up a sweat at the gym.

prompt.context_jp: After Etsuko admits she values appearance too, Yonekoka comments on her honesty.
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual comment sounds more natural for a coworker admiring Etsuko's frankness?

feedback.correct_en: 「正直だ」 is a na-adjective used predicatively; 「〜って〜だね」 is a natural casual topic+comment pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「正直をします」 treats 正直 as something you 'do' like an action noun, which is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: Convincing Fujiwa she shouldn't miss this once-in-a-lifetime chance.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for 'if you miss this, you may never get another chance'?

choices.text: これ逃したら、もう二度とないかもしれないよ。
これを逃げたら、もう二回ないかもしれないよ。

feedback.correct_en: 「逃す」 (miss an opportunity) is the right verb, and 「二度と〜ない」 is the idiomatic 'never again' phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「逃げる」 means 'run away/flee,' not 'miss a chance.' 「二回ない」 isn't the standard set phrase — it's 「二度と〜ない」.

prompt.context_jp: Morio describes how Etsuko can never hold her tongue.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural for 'she can't help saying what she thinks'?

choices.text: 思ったことを口にせずにはいられない。
思ったことを口にしないわけがない。

feedback.correct_en: 「〜ずにはいられない」 expresses an irresistible urge — exactly the 'can't help but say it' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「〜ないわけがない」 means 'there's no way she doesn't say it' (logical certainty), which sounds more like a deduction than a character trait.

contrast_examples.jp: 笑わずにはいられない。

contrast_examples.en: There's no way she doesn't know.
